mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES mobility signals more daily commuting and daytime presence in the city center, which raises retail and recreation visits with a four-week lag and lifts RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying above its t-1w level for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility toward baseline means fewer people staying at home, which mechanically shifts discretionary time into external activities and pushes RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 points above baseline after being above 12 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL drops below the stated threshold and stays there.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rises while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, leisure activity is shifting outdoors without restoring city-center access, so retail and recreation demand stays suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20 while TRANSIT stays below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains above 20 and TRANSIT remains below -40.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in TRANSIT above the recent trough indicates restored access to shopping and entertainment districts, and this access channel should raise RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a level below -45
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days of a TRANSIT increase that meets the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL implies precautionary, home-centered behavior that substitutes away from leisure shopping, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL are increasing together.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility marks weather or seasonal leisure substitution toward outdoor time, which diverts spending from retail venues and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to recover while TRANSIT remains depressed, commuting is shifting to non-transit modes and retail access stays incomplete, so RETAIL_REC should stay below the prior four-week average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -30 while TRANSIT remains below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the previous four-week mean even though WORKPLACES is above -30 and TRANSIT stays below -40.

mechanism_narrative: In a mobility normalization regime, the combination of rising GROCERY_PHARM and falling RESIDENTIAL indicates more out-of-home errands and less home confinement, which should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 7 days while GROCERY_PHARM increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases together.
